patches.value: Fix r≥0. Iterating the x matrix in F004 and dividing by r! gives X(r)e_i=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_(i−r)=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i. When r>i, iteration reaches x e_0=0 and gives zero. Similarly iteration of y gives Y(r)e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_(i+r)=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ, and gives zero past the terminating string. These binomial coefficients have nonnegative top at least r. They are integers: for every nonnegative integer a₀, the factorial expressions have boundary values binom(a₀,0)=binom(a₀,a₀)=1 and satisfy binom(a₀,s)=binom(a₀−1,s−1)+binom(a₀−1,s) for 0<s<a₀ by a common-denominator calculation. Induction on a₀, proving the assertion simultaneously for all 0≤s≤a₀, proves integrality. This establishes every divided-power formula in the exported conclusion as well as its zero cases.

Combining F004, or applying it to each e_k, gives X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_ij. Invert the coefficient using F003 to get E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F002 and R-linearity, hence every E_ij preserves M_R. With F002 and F003 this proves the entire statement the exported conclusion.

Choose ν_j,u_j from F006 and let ν be the minimum of the finite nonempty integer list ν_1,...,ν_k; choose j₀ attaining it. Such a minimum exists by repeatedly taking the smaller of two integers. Put b=p^ν a. This is nonzero, since p≠0 and a≠0. For each j, g_j=p^(ν_j−ν)u_j b lies in Rb because ν_j−ν≥0. Conversely g_(j₀)=u_(j₀)b, so b=u_(j₀)^(-1)g_(j₀) belongs to J. Thus the R-module generated by the g_j is exactly Rb, and J=Rb. Under F001, every vector of M_R is a sum Σ r_i b e_i, while any relation Σ r_i b e_i=0 has all r_i b=0 by the complex independence of e in N001, and hence all r_i=0. Thus (b e_i) is an R-basis. The same spanning and independence argument works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001, F002 and F004 this proves the exported conclusion.

Define Γ and Γ' by Γ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c and Γ'((r⊗m)⊗c)=m⊗φ(r)c. The defining ℤ-balancing relations in R⊗_ℤ M and in M⊗_ℤ K, and the R-balancing relation in M_R⊗_R K, show that these formulas extend to K-linear maps. They are inverse: Γ'Γ(m⊗c)=m⊗c, and ΓΓ'((r⊗m)⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗φ(r)c=(r⊗m)⊗c. These tensors generate, so the composites are identities. Next define Δ(z⊗c)=[z]⊗c and Δ'([z]⊗c)=z⊗c. Because p acts as zero on K, changing the lift z by pz' changes the second formula by pz'⊗c=z'⊗pc=0. Using F001, scalar balancing in F_p=R/pR gives the remaining balancing condition; thus both maps are well-defined and K-linear. Their composites are identities on pure tensors. This proves the two scalar-extension isomorphisms with exactly the formulas in the exported conclusion. An operator preserving M extends on all these tensors by applying it to the lattice factor; the displayed formulas commute with that operation. For Δ this also holds for any R-linear operator of M_R, since it preserves pM_R.

Fix 0≤r≤λ. As operators on M, the characteristic-zero definitions give r!X(r)=x^r and r!Y(r)=y^r; N002 gives their preservation of M. Tensoring these equalities gives the same equalities of induced operators on V_K. By F001, r!≠0 in K, so the induced divided powers equal (r!)^(-1)a^r and (r!)^(-1)d^r. The equality E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)Y(λ)X(λ)Y(λ−j) in N002 is an equality of R-linear operators on M_R. Extending scalars and transporting by Γ^(-1) preserves sums and compositions: this follows directly by evaluating on each pure tensor z⊗c. Substitute the divided-power equalities, whose indices λ−i, λ, λ−j all lie between 0 and λ. The result is T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)((λ−i)!)^(-1)a^(λ−i) (λ!)^(-1)d^λ (λ!)^(-1)a^λ ((λ−j)!)^(-1)d^(λ−j), with rightmost factor applied first. Every scalar inverse exists by F001. F004 gives T_ij β_k=δ_jk β_i. Along with F001–F004 this proves every assertion of the exported conclusion, including the two natural tensor identifications and positive dimension.

The alternatives W={0} and W≠{0} exhaust all cases. F002 and F004 therefore yield W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W to obtain the required assertion for every invariant K-subspace. N001 gives n=λ+1>0 and N004 gives a K-basis of V_K of that cardinality, so V_K is nonzero. The three generators span L_K, so their invariant subspaces are exactly L_K-submodules by K-linearity of ρ_K. H001 includes λ=0 and p=2: at λ=0 all powers and factorials used in T are zeroth powers and 1; if p=2 then λ is 0 or 1, and all preceding invertibilities still hold. No distinctness of h-eigenvalues in K was used; distinctness was used only over ℂ in N001. K was used solely as a field of characteristic p, so it need not be algebraically closed. This proves the full target the exported conclusion.
